descripcion: Two documentary pilot cases and six synthetic comparison cases for testing evidence-based justifications of coauthorship predictions. All authors and publications use local IDs.
procedencia: C001 and C002 retain their original documentary pilot data: overall classifications observed in the interface and keyword similarities calculated separately; the exact catalogue version used for the classifications is unknown. C003–C008 are entirely synthetic: authors, publications, scientific content and probabilities are fictional. Their keyword similarities are calculated from the synthetic keyword lists; no predictions were obtained from a real system for these six cases.

idiomas.criterio_evidencia: Preserve the source language of the pilot publications and the language in which each synthetic publication was written. Do not translate the evidence before sending it to the LLM. Responses are requested separately in Spanish and English.

instruccion_por_idioma.es: Redacta la justificación en español. Cita los artículos por su identificador local.
instruccion_por_idioma.en: Write the justification in English. Cite the articles by their local IDs.

nota_editorial: The scientific text of each abstract is reproduced in full. In P04, only the two author names in the final copyright notice are replaced with a bracketed label.

regla_coautoria.variable: Coauthorship probability supplied by the prediction method, from 0 to 1.
regla_coautoria.justificacion_propuesta: With calibrated probabilities and equal costs for false positives and false negatives, 0.50 is the point at which the two outcomes are equally likely. Assigning the tie to the favorable class is a pilot convention.
regla_coautoria.regla: Once a probability and a threshold are available for a method, classify the pair as favorable if its probability is at least the threshold and unfavorable otherwise. Leave the threshold-based classification unset if either value is missing.
regla_coautoria.justificacion_umbral_sintetico: For controlled tests, 0.50 separates simulated probabilities above and below the midpoint; if probabilities were calibrated and both error costs equal, this would be a reasonable starting rule. Equality is assigned to the favorable class by convention. The simulated values 0.85 and 0.15 are far from the threshold; 0.51 and 0.49 are equally close to it (0.01); 0.50 tests equality. These values are chosen for coverage, not estimated from data. The real threshold remains undefined.

publicaciones.titulo_original: Ultrasound Fetal Brain Registration Using Weighted Coherent Point Drift
publicaciones.abstract_original: Three dimensional ultrasound imaging has become the main modality for fetal health diagnostics, with extensive use in fetal brain imaging. According to the fetal position and the stage of development of the fetal skull, a specific plane of image acquisition is required. In most cases for a single plane of acquisition, the image quality is limited by the shadows produced by the skull. In this work a new method for registration of multiple views of 3D ultrasound of the fetal brain is reported, which results in improved imaging of the internal brain structures. In the initial stage, texture, intensity and edge features are used, with a support vector machine (SVM) for the segmentation of the skull in each of the 3D ultrasound views to be registered. The segmentation of each skull is modelled as a set of points with the centre determined with a Gaussian mixture model, where each point is assigned a probability of membership to a Gaussian determined by the posterior probability assigned by the SVM. Our method has shown improved results compared to intensity based registration, with a 52% reduction in the target registration error (TRE), and a 39% reduction in the TRE compared to feature based registration. These are encouraging results for the future development of an automatic method for registration and fusion of multiple views of 3D fetal ultrasound.
publicaciones.palabras_clave_originales: Automatic Registration; Support Vector Machine; Gaussian Mixture Model; Fetal Brain Imaging; Point Cloud Matching

publicaciones.titulo_original: Design and testing of a corpus for forensic speaker recognition using MFCC GMM and MLE
publicaciones.abstract_original: The importance of applying speaker recognition systems in forensic environments has increased in this century. One reason is the use of audio recordings as evidence in trials of every kind. This article presents a voice corpus design with this use in mind, based in recordings from speakers of the Spanish language dialect used in Central Mexico, distinct from any other corpus currently in use. For its evaluation, we used a Mel frequency Cepstral coefficient with a Gaussian Mixture Models for parametrization, and a Maximum Likelihood Estimation approach for classification. Results show an accuracy of more than 93% identification of the speaker at any condition, proving a good recognition model.
publicaciones.palabras_clave_originales: Mel frequency cepstral coefficient; Gaussian mixture model;Maximum likelihood estimation; Forensic speaker recognition;Speech corpus

referencia_evaluacion.afirmacion_respaldada: Both articles use Gaussian mixture models. P01 uses a Gaussian mixture model to determine the center of a point set during ultrasound image registration. P02 uses Gaussian mixture models for voice parametrization and maximum likelihood estimation for classification.
referencia_evaluacion.limite: The texts document a shared method across different applications. They do not establish which information drove the predictor or supply a probability of coauthorship.

publicaciones.titulo_original: A global model of the neural mechanisms responsible for visuomotor coordination in toads
publicaciones.abstract_original: A model of how the nervous system of toads processes visual information to control motor behaviour is proposed. The problem of visuomotor coordination in toads is studied through the integration of two different approaches: a top-down approach through schema theory developed in the studies of cognitive psychology, artificial intelligence and brain theory; and a bottom-up approach through the integration of physiological, anatomical, ethological, and neural modelling. The model proposes that visual information is processed in a parallel distributed way through different brain layers whose interaction defines the proper motor response for that specific situation. It is postulated that visual processing of information is organized into main schemata, which set the goal to be attained and, depending on the specific circumstances of the animal, activates different brain layers; the main schemata may use other schemata to solve a specific subproblem to reach the schema goal state. A schema is consistuted by perceptual and motor schemata, and a programme of schema co-ordination. With this model we have simulated how toads plan their route to reach a prey or the route to go away from a predator, depending on the state of their three-dimensional world. The model postulates specific hypotheses that could be tested experimentally on the processing of information in the toad's nervous system. © 1997 Elsevier Science Ltd. All rights reserved.

publicaciones.titulo_original: Designing Artificial Neural Networks Using Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithms
publicaciones.abstract_original: Artificial Neural Network (ANN) design is a complex task because its performance depends on the architecture, the selected transfer function, and the learning algorithm used to train the set of synaptic weights. In this paper we present a methodology that automatically designs an ANN using particle swarm optimization algorithms such as Basic Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Second Generation of Particle Swarm Optimization (SGPSO), and a New Model of PSO called NMPSO. The aim of these algorithms is to evolve, at the same time, the three principal components of an ANN: the set of synaptic weights, the connections or architecture, and the transfer functions for each neuron. Eight different fitness functions were proposed to evaluate the fitness of each solution and find the best design. These functions are based on the mean square error (MSE) and the classification error (CER) and implement a strategy to avoid overtraining and to reduce the number of connections in the ANN. In addition, the ANN designed with the proposed methodology is compared with those designed manually using the well-known Back-Propagation and Levenberg-Marquardt Learning Algorithms. Finally, the accuracy of the method is tested with different nonlinear pattern classification problems. © 2015 [author names omitted].
publicaciones.palabras_clave_originales: Algorithms;Back propagation;Complex networks;Learning algorithms;Mean square error;Network architecture;Neural networks

publicaciones.titulo_original: BM25 for retrieving technical reports in a university repository
publicaciones.abstract_original: University repositories contain technical reports with specialized terminology that is often absent from their titles. This study evaluates the BM25 ranking function for retrieving reports from a collection of computing and engineering documents. Titles and abstracts are indexed as a single textual field. A set of technical queries is used to compare BM25 rankings with rankings obtained from unweighted term counts. Relevance is assessed by examining whether the retrieved reports address the information requested in each query. The analysis focuses on the effect of document length and term frequency on the order of the retrieved reports.
publicaciones.palabras_clave_originales: BM25; Information retrieval; Document ranking; Academic repositories

publicaciones.titulo_original: Ranking research articles with BM25 in a digital library
publicaciones.abstract_original: Searching research articles by subject requires identifying documents whose terminology corresponds to the information need. This study applies BM25 to rank research articles using their titles and abstracts. Queries are formulated from research topics and the retrieved articles are assessed for relevance. Different document length normalization settings are examined to determine their effect on ranking. Unlike a retrieval system based only on exact title matches, the proposed experiment considers terms that occur in abstracts. The study examines retrieval quality in a digital library without using author collaboration data.
publicaciones.palabras_clave_originales: BM25; Information retrieval; Document ranking; Digital libraries

publicaciones.titulo_original: Query optimization with composite indexes in relational databases
publicaciones.abstract_original: This study examines the execution of selection and join queries in relational databases. Composite indexes are created on attributes frequently used together in filtering conditions. Query execution plans are inspected to compare access paths with and without these indexes. The experiments measure query execution time and index storage requirements as the number of database records increases. The objective is to identify conditions under which composite indexes reduce the cost of database queries. No biological measurements or image processing methods are used in the experiments.
publicaciones.palabras_clave_originales: Relational databases; Composite indexes; Query optimization; Execution plans

publicaciones.titulo_original: Measuring leaf water loss using controlled humidity chambers
publicaciones.abstract_original: Leaf water loss is studied under controlled environmental conditions. Samples of leaves are placed in humidity chambers and their mass is measured at fixed intervals. Air temperature and relative humidity are varied independently to examine their effects on water loss. Differences between samples are compared using the measured change in mass over time. The objective is to describe the response of plant tissues to environmental conditions using direct physical measurements. The study does not develop database queries or evaluate database indexing methods.

publicaciones.titulo_original: Support vector machines for classifying research project descriptions
publicaciones.abstract_original: This study examines automatic classification of research project descriptions into predefined computing areas. Each description is represented by a vector of term frequency–inverse document frequency weights. A linear support vector machine is trained on descriptions assigned to areas by human reviewers. Classification performance is examined using a held-out set of descriptions, with particular attention to errors between closely related computing areas. The aim is to determine whether the textual descriptions can support automatic assignment of project areas.
publicaciones.palabras_clave_originales: Support vector machine; TF-IDF; Text classification; Research projects

publicaciones.titulo_original: Subject classification of scientific abstracts using linear support vector machines
publicaciones.abstract_original: Scientific abstracts are classified into predefined subject categories using a linear support vector machine. Words in the abstracts are represented with term frequency–inverse document frequency weights calculated from the training collection. The classifier is evaluated using labeled abstracts not included in training. Errors are examined to determine whether overlapping subject terminology makes certain categories difficult to distinguish. The aim is to support subject-based access to scientific publications.

publicaciones.titulo_original: Detección de cambios en series de consumo eléctrico mediante PELT
publicaciones.abstract_original: El estudio examina cambios en el consumo eléctrico horario de edificios universitarios. Se utiliza el algoritmo PELT para localizar puntos de cambio en la media de las series de consumo. Se comparan distintas penalizaciones y se revisa si los puntos detectados corresponden a cambios en los patrones de ocupación. La finalidad es identificar periodos con características de consumo distintas sin clasificar previamente cada hora. El análisis se realiza por edificio y no incluye información de colaboraciones académicas.
publicaciones.palabras_clave_originales: PELT; Puntos de cambio; Series temporales; Consumo eléctrico

publicaciones.titulo_original: Detección de cambios en tiempos de respuesta de servidores mediante PELT
publicaciones.abstract_original: Este trabajo analiza series temporales de tiempos de respuesta de servidores. El algoritmo PELT se aplica para detectar puntos de cambio en la media de los tiempos registrados. Se examina el efecto de la penalización sobre el número de puntos detectados y se contrastan los cambios con registros de carga de trabajo. El objetivo es identificar periodos con distintos niveles de respuesta del servicio. El estudio no utiliza mediciones de consumo eléctrico.

publicaciones.titulo_original: Topic grouping of scientific abstracts with non-negative matrix factorization
publicaciones.abstract_original: This study groups scientific abstracts into topics by applying non-negative matrix factorization to a document-term matrix. The matrix contains non-negative term weights derived from the abstracts. Each factor is interpreted using the terms with the largest weights and representative documents are inspected to assess the topic. The number of factors is varied to examine how it affects the resulting groups. The objective is to organize a collection of scientific abstracts by subject without assigning categories in advance.
publicaciones.palabras_clave_originales: Non-negative matrix factorization; Topic modeling; Document-term matrix; Scientific abstracts

publicaciones.titulo_original: Agrupación temática de informes técnicos mediante factorización matricial no negativa
publicaciones.abstract_original: Este trabajo estudia la agrupación de informes técnicos por tema mediante factorización matricial no negativa. Se construye una matriz de documentos y términos con pesos no negativos obtenidos del texto de los informes. Los temas se interpretan mediante los términos de mayor peso en cada factor y se revisan documentos representativos. Se analiza cómo cambia la agrupación al variar el número de factores. El objetivo es organizar informes por tema sin utilizar etiquetas previas.
publicaciones.palabras_clave_originales: Factorización matricial no negativa; Modelado de temas; Matriz de documentos y términos; Informes técnicos

publicaciones.titulo_original: Random forest classification of network traffic records
publicaciones.abstract_original: This study evaluates random forest classification of network traffic records. Features are extracted from packet counts, connection duration and transferred data volume. A random forest is trained to distinguish normal traffic from previously labeled abnormal traffic. The evaluation uses records held out from training and examines the types of errors made by the classifier. The objective is to assess whether the selected traffic features support the identification of abnormal connections.

publicaciones.titulo_original: Classifying sensor operating conditions using random forests
publicaciones.abstract_original: This study evaluates a random forest classifier for identifying operating conditions from sensor measurements. Features are extracted from measurements of temperature, vibration and current. The classifier is trained using observations labeled with normal and abnormal operating conditions. A separate test set is used to examine classification errors for the operating conditions. The aim is to assess the usefulness of the sensor features for distinguishing normal operation from abnormal behavior.
